texts: On VV-ECMO the pulmonary vascular bed is perfused with oxygen-rich blood: C.
Blood is drained from the venous side, oxygenated and returned to the right atrium, so the right ventricle pumps already oxygenated blood through the lungs, which relaxes the pulmonary vessels.
The heart does all the pumping, so pulsatile flow is preserved, and the coronary arteries receive this oxygenated blood from the left ventricle, so the myocardium is well oxygenated.
In children a single double-lumen cannula is preferred, and the lungs are rested on gentle ventilator settings, not collapsed.
In the picture, the water leaving the gills is already bright red before it reaches the pipes of dollar bills.
Memory hook: with gills on the vein, the money pipes run red.
